interface.title: Haku - protein structure navigator
interface.stage_of_work: Looking up existing data before or during structure analysis: finding which experimental structures, papers, ligands, annotations and residue-number mappings already exist for a protein, then handing them to PyMOL
interface.what_it_is_for: Enter a UniProt accession or PDB code(s) and get live tables from UniProt, PDBe and Europe PMC: structures, papers, protein chains, ligands, transmembrane annotation shown on a 3D structure, sequence alignment and SIFTS mappings, plus PyMOL command snippets to copy into your own session.

data.note: Each page comes with a default query already filled in (Q9NR09; 9eii 9eij 9eih; 7UPI ... 7SD0; Q63008 + 7UV0; 8qoi; 9i1w / La / G0SGT6). All results are fetched live from UniProt, PDBe and Europe PMC, and each page takes 30 s to several minutes to respond. Nothing was uploaded. Every result in the tree comes from the default inputs, apart from the hand-typed TM annotation.

tree.specific: Use Haku to go from a UniProt AC or PDB codes to structure lists, literature, protein chains, ligands, TM topology, sequence alignment, SIFTS DBREF records and PyMOL commands

features.name: Identifier-to-records lookup with 'not yet indexed' flagging
features.general: Enter one identifier, get a table of all linked records, and see highlighted which records are recent and not yet in the curated database, plus a ready list of IDs to copy
features.specific: Enter a UniProt AC and press Fetch data to get a PDB/PMID table; rows not yet in UniProt are highlighted; separate 'Available in UniProt' and 'Not yet available' PDB lists, each with a copyable code block
steps: type UniProt AC in sidebar
press Fetch data
read the PDB/PMID table with highlighted rows
copy the space-separated PDB code list
serves_tasks: Find every structure and associated paper for one protein identifier

features.name: Linked literature table
features.general: For a set of records, list the associated publications (ID, title, year, journal), with links out, a highlight marking papers already curated in the reference database, and a table toolbar for search, column toggling and export
features.specific: Associated literature (PMIDs) table built from Europe PMC, with Europe PMC links and the Streamlit dataframe toolbar. Highlighted rows here are PMIDs curated in UniProt. This is the opposite of the structure table, where a highlight means 'not yet in UniProt'
steps: fetch data for a UniProt AC
jump to 'Associated literature' from the sidebar
read which PMIDs are highlighted as curated in UniProt
hover the table to reveal the toolbar
search or hide columns (Download as CSV produced no file in this run)
serves_tasks: Find every structure and associated paper for one protein identifier

features.name: Multi-structure component and ligand inventory
features.general: Enter several structure IDs, analyse them one by one with a progress bar, and get one combined table of components, small molecules and quality metrics, plus de-duplicated lists of proteins, ligands and entries
features.specific: List the proteins: PDB codes, then the Proteins and ligands table (Entity, Chain, UniProt AC/ID, HETATM, Resolution, Method), then the UniProt list, Ligands/Modifications and PDB list
steps: type space- or comma-separated PDB codes
press Analyse structure and watch 'Analysing X (n/N)'
read the combined table
jump between the UniProt, Ligand and PDB lists with sidebar anchors
serves_tasks: For several structure IDs, list their protein components, resolution, method and bound small molecules

features.name: Viewer-script generator from the analysed set
features.general: Turn the analysis result into a copy-paste script that loads all entries and colours and names each component across them
features.specific: The PyMOL Commands block: 'fetch' line plus util.cbaw / 'sele TOM20_HUMAN, (chain D and 9eii) or ...' / util.cnc, with a copy icon on hover and a link to Other PyMOL Commands
steps: run Analyse structure
jump to 'PyMOL commands'
hover the code block and press copy
optionally open Other PyMOL Commands
serves_tasks: Generate a script that loads the structures and colours and labels each protein
Browse a reference list of general-purpose viewer commands

features.name: Editable region annotation painted on a 3D model
features.general: Show the reference database's region annotation coloured on a rotatable 3D structure; next to it, edit the regions as text, re-render the model, and export matching colour commands for an external viewer
features.specific: TM annotations: UniProt FT TRANSMEM lines shown on py3Dmol with an Outside/Inside key; a 'Manual annotation' textarea with Update annotation re-colours a second viewer (only TRANSMEM lines were coloured; TOPO_DOM lines were not); entering a PDB/model name produces 'util.cbaw ...; color 31, <model> and resi a-b' commands
steps: enter UniProt AC + PDB code (Fetch data / Show structure)
inspect the UniProt-coloured structure
edit FT TRANSMEM / TOPO_DOM lines in the textarea
press Update annotation to re-colour
type a model name to generate PyMOL commands
serves_tasks: Show the database's transmembrane segments coloured on the 3D model
Edit the topology by hand, re-render it, and export it as viewer commands

features.name: Chain-to-reference pairwise alignment card
features.general: Given a structure chain and a reference sequence ID, show both records side by side with copy buttons, summary metrics (identity, coverage, overlap, gap frequency, score) and a numbered alignment with match markers
features.specific: Align sequences: PDB code + chain ID + UniProt AC, then Align sequences, giving Structure and Protein cards, Copy PDB/UniProt sequence buttons, metric chips and a BLOSUM62 local alignment
steps: enter PDB code, chain ID and UniProt AC
press Align sequences
read the identity/coverage chips and the aligned range
optionally copy either sequence
serves_tasks: Align one chain's sequence to its reference protein sequence and read identity and coverage

features.name: Residue-mapping export in a standard record format
features.general: Fetch the mapping between structure chains and reference sequences, show summary counts, render it as fixed-format records and download it as a text file
features.specific: Fetch SIFTS mappings: PDB code, then a header card, chips (records/chains/uniprot/merged), syntax-highlighted DBREF lines and a 'Download dbref.txt' button
steps: enter a PDB code
press Fetch SIFTS mappings
check the record/chain/merged counts
press Download dbref.txt
serves_tasks: Fetch the per-chain mapping to the reference database as a standard text record and save it
